name: Z-spider copies the W unit
summary: The state |0⟩ (a W-node without outputs) is copied by a phase-free Z-spider.
description:
A W-node with no outputs is the state $|0\rangle$ (read as an effect, it is $\langle 0|$), which is the unit of the W-node read as a 'merge'.

A phase-free Z-spider sends $|0\rangle$ to $|0\cdots0\rangle$, so plugging the unit of the W-node into it gives a copy of the unit on every output. Together with the [W/Z bialgebra](../w-z-bialgebra/) and the [Z/W Hopf rule](../zw-hopf/) this is one of the axioms saying that the W-node and the Z-spider form a (Hopf-like) bialgebra: axiom 6b of Hadzihasanovic's original complete ZW-calculus. It is the ZW-version of the [state copy](../state-copy/) rule of the ZX-calculus, with the $|0\rangle$ state drawn as a W-node instead of an X-spider.
parameter_notes: Shown for a Z-spider with two outputs; holds for any number of outputs.
